sources.name: WiCAN (MeatPi) OBD-II adapter
sources.status: active; last commit 2026-11-23; 134 stars; README carries 'HACS Default' badge
sources.last_release: not checked (GitHub API blocked; date = last commit of shallow clone)
sources.access: Hardware OBD-II/CAN dongle on car Wi-Fi/home Wi-Fi. Device runs AutoPID protocol with a per-vehicle profile and pushes to HA (webhook/HTTP API; integration says 'WiCAN does not poll the vehicle from Home Assistant'). Alternative: firmware publishes to MQTT with HA discovery (docs conflict on whether MQTT discovery is currently enabled: not verified). Data only while the car is awake and in Wi-Fi range.
sources.notes: Verified in source for the HACS integration. Sensors are DYNAMIC: one per PID name configured on the device; unique_id = f'{entry_id}_pid_{pid_key}'; no translation_key. PID names are conventions from the vehicle profile (integration data/params.json has 337 known names with unit/class) but users can define their own, so treat as user-defined. Availability of each PID depends on the vehicle profile.

sources.region: worldwide; mostly EVs (Leaf, Twizy, Zoe, i3, MG, Smart, VW e-Up ...)
sources.notes: Verified in source (metrics/common/*.py). Entities are created from MQTT topics, key = OVMS metric name; names from a metric table; unique_id namespaced 'ovms_{entry_id}_...'. No translation_key found. Only vehicles whose OVMS module decodes a metric publish it. This is the ONLY brand-neutral source with a real 'distance/time to service' metric.

service_distance.note: name 'Service Distance'; 'Distance to next scheduled maintenance/service'; diagnostic

service_time.note: time/date of next service (OVMS docs: timestamp, guess)

tyres.note: exact v.tp keys not grepped in metrics/common: guess from OVMS metric list

sources.name: Traccar Server
sources.last_release: core
sources.access: Self-hosted/cloud Traccar GPS server; many cheap OBD/GPS trackers report to it. local/cloud polling + websocket.
sources.notes: Verified in core source: NO odometer / totalDistance / hours sensor. Fixed sensors: attributes.batteryLevel, attributes.power (tk 'power', V = external/vehicle supply), attributes.battery (tk 'battery', V = tracker battery), speed, altitude, address, geofence. But the options flow has 'custom attributes' (CONF_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES) which copy any Traccar position attribute (e.g. totalDistance, odometer, hours) into the device_tracker's state attributes: user must add a template sensor. So odometer = attribute, user-defined.

prior_art.name: LubeLogger + lubelogger-ha
prior_art.repo: https://github.com/hargata/lubelog (app, 2981 stars, pushed 2026-11-19); https://github.com/hollowpnt92/lubelogger-ha (HACS, ref fdd960f, 16 stars, last commit 2026-01-05, manifest 1.0.13)
prior_art.status: app very active; HA integration small and slow-moving. No other LubeLogger HA integration found.
prior_art.what: Self-hosted web vehicle maintenance + fuel tracker (service/repair/upgrade records, odometer log, taxes, supplies, plans, reminders by date, mileage or whichever comes first). The HA integration polls its REST API (/api/vehicle/odometerrecords, adjustedodometer, reminders, servicerecords, gasrecords, planrecords ...) and makes one device per vehicle. Read-only: verified in source, no services to push an odometer.
prior_art.entities: sensor keys (unique_id lubelogger_{vehicle_id}_{key}, names not translated): latest_odometer (DISTANCE, unit HARD-CODED 'mi', state_class measurement), next_reminder (TIMESTAMP = dueDate, whole reminder record as attributes), next_plan (TIMESTAMP), latest_service / latest_repair / latest_upgrade / latest_supply / latest_gas (TIMESTAMP, record in attributes), latest_tax (MONETARY, hard-coded USD)
prior_art.lesson: Expose 'next due' as proper typed entities with numeric distance/days remaining (not a blob of attributes with hard-coded units), and consider LubeLogger as an optional import/export target rather than competing with its logbook.

prior_art.name: Maintenance Supporter
prior_art.what: Generic home maintenance tracker with sensor triggers (threshold, counter/delta, runtime, state-change, compound), objects nested in objects ('both cars inside Vehicles'), spare parts, To-do entity. HAS VEHICLE FEATURES: helpers/signatures/cars.py is a source-verified catalog of 39 car/bike integrations (kia_uvo, tesla_custom, renault, mbapi2020, volvo, fordpass, toyota, myskoda, audiconnect, tesla_fleet, teslemetry, tessie, ituran, starline, stellantis_vehicles, cardata, porscheconnect, nissan_connect, smartcar, abrp, volkswagencarnet, smarthashtag, byd_vehicle, dvla, pycupra, ...) mapping translation_keys to suggested tasks.
prior_art.entities: Matches other integrations' entities by registry translation_key with entity_id-suffix / original_name fallback. Car task templates seen: 'Annual Service' from odometer (usage_delta 15000 km) or from countdown keys (distance_to_service / service_inspection_distance value_below 1000; days_to_service / service_inspection_days below 336 h), 'Tire Rotation' (odometer delta 10000), 'Oil Service' (oil % percent_left; oil_inspection_days/distance).
prior_art.lesson: Direct prior art for car_keeper's source catalog: match by translation_key (rename-proof) with fallbacks, record source+verified ref per signature, and distinguish countdown signals (car knows) from odometer-delta (we compute); differentiate by going deeper on cars than its two or three generic tasks.

prior_art.name: Vehicle Service Manager
prior_art.status: small, German-only UI strings, HACS custom repo
prior_art.what: Per-vehicle service intervals by km and months with preset defaults, first-registration date as baseline until a service is logged, tyre tread-depth tracking, service log via service add_service_entry(vehicle_id, entry_date, km, services). Odometer is fed by an automation calling a service from e.g. sensor.obd_odometer (README) or typed manually.
prior_art.entities: per service: sensor '{vehicle_id}_{svc}_status' (attributes last_service_km, km_left, months_left, interval_km, interval_months) and binary_sensor '{vehicle_id}_{svc}_due' (device_class problem); binary_sensor '{vehicle_id}_any_due'; sensor '{vehicle_id}_km' (Kilometerstand, km); sensor '{vehicle_id}_tire_{position}' (mm tread depth)
prior_art.lesson: Per-task due binary_sensor + one 'any due' roll-up + registration date as initial baseline are good patterns; avoid km-only units, hard-coded German names and needing a user automation to feed the odometer (link the source entity directly).

prior_art.name: CARnet (ha-carnet-entretien)
prior_art.status: active, French origin, HACS custom integration with its own card
prior_art.what: Maintenance logbook for cars, motorcycles, scooters, e-bikes: hard-coded maintenance catalog per vehicle category with intervals refined by engine/trim, mileage typed manually or taken from a linked HA sensor (service set_mileage_source), notifications when due by time or mileage, recalls, known issues, cost estimates, resale value, invoices, PDF history; uses a Gemini client (cloud LLM) for some data. Services: add_vehicle, update_mileage, set_mileage_source, log_maintenance, refresh_plan, refresh_known_issues, refresh_recalls, value_snapshot, remove_vehicle.
prior_art.entities: Only 3 sensors per vehicle (unique_id carnet_entretien_{vehicle_id}_{suffix}): NextMaintenanceSensor, MileageSensor (km), ResaleValueSensor (EUR); everything else lives in the custom card/storage.
prior_art.lesson: Closest competitor in scope: copy the linked-odometer-or-manual model and built-in catalog, but expose every task as an entity (it hides them in a card), stay local (no LLM/cloud dependency) and support mi/other currencies.

prior_art.name: AutoLog add-on
prior_art.status: small add-on (not an integration); facts from the author's forum post only
prior_art.what: Fuel-up, running-cost and maintenance logbook as an add-on with SQLite; one MQTT device per vehicle; imports Fuelly/Fuelio/Drivvo CSV; command topic to log a fill-up from an automation.
prior_art.entities: ten MQTT-discovered sensors per vehicle with state_class (names not listed in the post: not verified)
prior_art.lesson: CSV import from the common fuel-log apps is the realistic bridge for history; an add-on is the wrong shape for entity-first HA users.

prior_art.name: Drivvo / Spritmonitor integrations (log apps with reminders)
prior_art.what: Mirror a cloud fuel-log account into HA, including the app's own service reminders.
prior_art.entities: Drivvo: odometer (tk odometer_value), service_odometer, service_date, reminder_next_distance, reminder_next_days, reminder_next_date, reminders_overdue, binary_sensor maintenance_due (problem). Spritmonitor: last_refuel_odometer, next_service_km, km_to_next_service, next_service_date, next_service_note.
prior_art.lesson: The entity triple 'distance remaining / days remaining / due flag' is the de-facto shape users already see; log-app odometers are stale (last fill-up), so accept them only as a low-priority odometer source.

prior_art.name: Generic chore/maintenance helpers (Chore Helper, Device Maintenance Monitor, Home Maintenance, Activity Manager)
prior_art.repo: https://github.com/VolantisDev/ha-chore-helper (157 stars, pushed 2026-01-26); https://github.com/rafael-zilberman/device-maintenance-monitor-custom-component (21 stars, pushed 2025-01-13); others not located
prior_art.status: not cloned; from repo descriptions only (guess)
prior_art.what: Time-based recurring chores, or runtime/count-based device maintenance; no vehicle or odometer features found.
prior_art.lesson: Time-only schedulers cannot express 'whichever comes first: km or months', which is the core of car maintenance: that dual trigger is car_keeper's reason to exist.
